Text: Fewer enemies, the Guards are automatically restored to 4 after each level, and achievements cannot be unlocked.
Same balance as Normal, but the game starts with only one Guard.
Grandmaster difficulty is unlocked only after\nsuccessfully completing Campaign Mode on Normal difficulty.
The following law is in effect for this level:
No special rules. Standard chess movement rules apply.
Guards can move only vertically or horizontally.
Only the three directions that include forward movement are allowed.
Guards can move only sideways or diagonally sideways; no straight forward or backward movement.
Once per guard per level, a 2-square orthogonal move is allowed if both squares are clear.
Once per guard per level, a 2-square diagonal move is allowed if both squares are clear.
Each guard's first move can cover 2 squares in the same direction if the path is clear.
Each guard must alternate between orthogonal and diagonal movement.
A guard cannot repeat the same direction as its previous move.
One of the 8 directions is chosen at random and remains forbidden for the entire level.
Once per level, one guard can move 2 squares in any direction if the path is clear.
After a diagonal move, that guard cannot be selected on the next turn.
Each guard's first orthogonal move causes no enemy response.
Guards cannot end their move on a road-edge square.
Once per guard, you may jump over an adjacent piece and land on the square immediately beyond it.
When a guard reaches the checkered checkpoint, the player may keep playing for five consecutive turns.
Enemy Knights cannot end their move on a white square.
You cannot select the same guard on two consecutive turns.
Every active guard must move once before any of them can move again.
Each turn, the game randomly indicates which guard must move, provided it has a legal move.
Once per level, you can make two consecutive moves before the enemy response.
Every fifth guard move skips the enemy response.
Every fifth guard move grants the enemy two consecutive moves.
For the first three enemy responses, enemies cannot move or capture.
After a capture, the same guard may immediately move a second time, once per turn.
If only one active guard remains, it gets two moves before each enemy response.
While all 4 guards are alive, enemies move only after every 2 player moves.
Every four guard moves, enemies can make two consecutive moves.
Once per level, freeze all visible enemies for one turn.
The first hit that would eliminate a guard is ignored.
A guard cannot end more than 3 squares away from the nearest guard.
Two guards cannot end their moves on adjacent squares.
Two guards cannot occupy the same column.
Every 3 turns, one of the most advanced guards must move.
One random guard is marked and must remain within 1 square of the road's center line.
One random guard must make at least one capture before it can cross the checkpoint.
Two random guards must remain within 2 squares of each other.
After a guard is lost, the next move may cover 2 squares.
A marked guard cannot be captured while adjacent to another active guard.
Enemy Knights remain still and cannot capture.
Knights prefer the legal move that brings them closer to the nearest guard.
Bring a guard back to life by moving onto the indicated square. The resurrected guard will start from the starting row.
Bishops choose a legal move at random within their range.
Mobile enemy pieces may choose only moves that bring them closer to the bottom edge of the screen.
Mobile enemy pieces may choose only moves that take them farther from the bottom edge.
Enemies must remain in the left or right half of the grid where they started the level.
Enemy Rooks move and capture only diagonally, like Bishops.
Only one randomly selected enemy type among those present can move or capture; all others remain still.
The opponent cannot choose the same piece on two consecutive responses if another piece can move.
Enemy Knights can jump only two columns and one row.
If a Rook can capture, the opponent must choose a Rook capture.
Long-range enemies cannot capture from a distance of one square.
Long-range enemies can capture only from a distance of one square.
Distant enemies appear as "?" or "!" symbols until they are within 6 rows.
After an attack, that enemy cannot attack on the next enemy response.
All ranged pieces reduce their range by 5.
Every 15 guard moves, a random enemy Pawn transforms into a Knight.
Reduces the number of enemies in the level by 25%.
Increases the number of enemies in the level by 25%.
No enemy can be generated in the first 4 walkable rows.
At least one enemy is generated in the 3 rows before the checkpoint.
Enemies are generated preferentially on road-edge squares.
No enemy can be generated adjacent to another enemy.
Enemies prefer to appear within 2 squares of another enemy.
The first time a guard reaches halfway up the route, an enemy Pawn appears on a valid empty square.
Enemies placed in the upper half of the road are all Pawns.
The road is 2 columns wider than normal.
The road is 2 columns narrower than normal, with a safe minimum width.
Reduces the probability of bends almost to zero.
Increases the probability of changing direction by 50%.
The road tends to alternate left and right bends.
Generates 2 bottlenecks, each one row long.
The road shifts sideways by one column at regular intervals.
Forces one large S-shaped bend in the level.
The road's center line shifts abruptly once.
Guards can enter the checkpoint only with a diagonal move.
If you enter a magenta square, you will exit from the cyan square with the same number, and vice versa. However, teleportation is possible only if the two squares are not both occupied.
The valid checkpoint square shifts by one column every 2 turns.
In this level, the Guards move like knights.
15 random magenta safe squares protect any guards occupying them from captures.
Generates 10 impassable purple squares on the road.
Fifteen blocks are present at the start; one is removed every four player moves.
Marked tiles can only be crossed by Guards using diagonal moves.
Every square occupied by a Knight becomes inaccessible once that Knight moves away from it.
Valid checkpoint squares alternate between active and inactive every turn.
At the start of the white turn, the enemy closest to a guard is indicated and will act if it has a legal move.
Distant enemies appear as '?' symbols until they are within 4 rows.

At the start of the level, a random tile appears with a magenta number starting at 5 and decreasing after every Guard move. When it reaches zero, the tile explodes, removes any piece on it, and becomes unusable. A new tile with the same effect then appears.
Enemy Pawns cannot capture a Guard standing on a black square.
Rooks and Bishops can move only up to a maximum distance of 5 squares.
Rooks and Bishops can move only up to a maximum distance of 2 squares.
Rooks and Bishops can move only up to a maximum distance of 1 square.
The first capture of the level causes no enemy response.
Every capture triggers one extra enemy response.
Guards cannot capture and must avoid all enemies.
A guard that captures cannot capture again for its next 2 moves.
If a guard captures and can capture again from there, it may immediately do so once.
During the Guards' odd-numbered shifts, all enemies become invisible, but they can still capture and be captured.
One random enemy cannot be captured.
Each guard's first capture is free; subsequent captures trigger one extra enemy response.
Every fourth team move may cover two orthogonal squares along a clear path.
Every fifth team move must be diagonal.
After the player's tenth move, long-range enemies gain one extra move.
Enemies are concentrated in two separate bands.
In this level, Guards and Enemies transform into whatever they have just captured.
Each guard that reaches the checkpoint cancels the next enemy response, if the level continues.
The final third of the road is generated one column narrower and with only its initial enemies.
The road is 1 column narrower, but the first hit suffered by the team is ignored.
The road is more winding, but enemies respond only after every 2 moves.
Each guard has one Dash, but cannot be selected twice in a row.
10 blocked squares, but also 10 cyan safe squares.
Enemies chase the nearest guard, but move only on alternating turns.
After every full turn, the Royal Guard and the enemy Queen are transformed into a random chess piece.
